item.title: Europe Sees Modest Growth, But The Weaker US Dollar Looms As A Threat
item.description: By DAVID McHUGH AP Business Writer FRANKFURT, Germany (AP) — The European economy recorded modest growth at the end of last year, pushing past turmoil over higher U.S. tariffs. Now the economy faces another hurdle: a stronger euro against the dollar that could weigh on exports. Growth in the 21 countries that use the shared euro currency came in at 0.3% for the last three months of 2025, matching the figure from the third quarter, the EU statistics agency Eurostat reported Friday. item.title: Venezuela’s Acting President Signs Oil Industry Overhaul, Easing State Control To Lure Investors
item.description: By REGINA GARCIA CANO Associated Press CARACAS, Venezuela (AP) — Venezuela’s acting President Delcy Rodríguez on Thursday signed a law that opens the nation’s oil sector to privatization, reversing a tenet of the self-proclaimed socialist movement that has ruled the country for more than two decades. item.title: Trump Impeachment Promise
item.description: Congresswoman Jasmine Crockett is telling Texas voters that, if elected to the Senate, she’ll support impeachment proceedings against President Trump. Experts say this is a gift to Republicans. Political strategist James Dickey says that most voters here support the president. New polling out this week has Congresswoman Crockett in a dead heat with State Representative James Talarico with less than three weeks until early voting begins.

item.title: Power Grid Thrives
item.description: This week’s Arctic blast tested the state’s power grid, but experts say it passed. Tom Overbye at the Smart Grid Center says that work over the past five years has hardened transmission lines, so they can handle a freeze. Also, he says more power generation has come online since Winter Storm Uri, allowing the grid to keep up with demand.

item.title: Summer Camp Safety
item.description: A coalition of nearly 160 Texas summer camps is warning that operations may be canceled due to safety requirements passed after last year’s deadly flooding. State Rep Wes Virdell, who represents the area, blasted his fellow lawmakers for mandating high-speed internet service when the infrastructure isn’t there. The Department of State Health Services is set to release specific requirements by early February, along with a schedule for camps.

item.title: AG Lawsuit Dismissed
item.description: A lawsuit filed by Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton was so full of lies that a federal judge has issued a rare “bad faith” ruling. item.title: ICE Tracker Website
item.description: Two students at Rice University in Houston have created an interactive map to track ICE operations across the country. But questions are being raised about it’s legality. Chris Russo, who heads the group Texans for Strong Borders, says it facilitates attacks on ICE agents. The map also shows the location of immigrant detention facilities and points out if they have documented health and security inspection failures.
